description: Unchanged normalized authored stage pairs exposing clause-container, attracting-head and successive-source ambiguities in movement recovery.

cases.name: archive-english-raising-xbar-astra-0
cases.sentence: Mia seems to want to leave.

values.commitment: Finite I is abstract and silent; no separate affix or head-movement step is represented.
values.form: seems is the whole-word present-tense third-person singular form.

requirements: The matrix EPP requires an occupied subject position.
The matrix subject position bears no theta-role.

values.interpretation: PRO is obligatorily interpreted as Mia.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge seems with the existing want IP and project the matrix VP and finite IP. Seems is a raising predicate: it selects an infinitival IP, assigns no external theta-role, and provides no accusative Case for that infinitive's subject. Unlike the CP selected by want, this IP contains no intervening CP boundary blocking subject raising. The matrix subject position is not yet occupied. Finite I supplies the nominative licensing position that Mia needs, but Mia still occupies the embedded subject position in this workspace. The tree treats seems as a whole-word, lexically inflected V licensed by abstract finite I; it does not posit separate pronounced affix pieces or V-to-I movement. The remaining step is therefore NP raising, not verb movement.
derivationStages.statement: Build the finite raising clause above the want infinitive.

values.operation: Move NP from embedded Spec-IP to matrix Spec-IP.

values.condition: The chain has one theta-role, assigned at its foot; seems assigns no external theta-role.

values.EPP: satisfied by Mia in matrix Spec-IP

conditions: The antecedent c-commands and antecedent-governs the trace.
The A-trace is bound in its governing domain.
No intervening CP barrier or subject blocks raising.

relations.relation: obligatory subject control through the A-chain

values.interpretation: The subject chain of want controls PRO, so Mia is understood as the leaver.

values.condition: PRO remains ungoverned in the control CP and is not a member of the raising chain.

values.interpretation: It seems that Mia wants to leave.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Move Mia from the previously represented Spec-IP of want to matrix Spec-IP, leaving a silent NP trace in the embedded subject position. The raised NP and its trace form one A-chain: its foot retains the Experiencer theta-role assigned by want, while its head receives nominative Case from finite I and satisfies the matrix EPP. This movement crosses no intervening subject or CP barrier; the raised NP c-commands and antecedent-governs its trace. Seems contributes no additional subject theta-role. The local subject position of want, now occupied by the trace, continues to determine control of the lower PRO through the Mia chain. PRO itself has not moved and independently receives the Agent role of leave. Thus the analysis combines raising over want with control into leave, rather than treating want as another raising verb. The final structure licenses the exact input: Mia appears to have the desire to leave. The sentence is grammatical under the Theta Criterion, Case Filter, binding requirements on the A-trace, and the PRO theorem.
derivationStages.statement: Raise Mia to the finite subject position and complete the grammatical analysis.

cases.name: fresh-raising-other-framework-0
cases.sentence: The sailors seem to have reached the island.

values.morphologicalTreatment: whole-word lexical inflection without overt V-to-I movement

derivationStages.stageRecord: Seem selects the existing infinitival IP and projects V-bar and VP. A silent finite I supplies present tense, and the resulting I-bar projects to matrix IP, whose specifier has not yet been filled. Seem is a raising predicate: it assigns no external theta-role and therefore supplies no thematic matrix subject position. Its propositional complement is the infinitival IP, not a CP; there is no complementizer projection intervening in the subsequent raising dependency. The present-tense verb is represented by the ordinary whole-word terminal seem, licensed by abstract finite I. This analysis assumes lexical inflection with no overt V-to-I movement or separately pronounced tense affix. Number agreement will be established when the matrix subject position is filled.
derivationStages.statement: Embed the infinitival IP under seem and construct the finite matrix projection.

values.interpretation: one theta-role assigned at the foot of the A-chain

values.locality: transparent raising IP with no intervening CP barrier

derivationStages.stageRecord: The sailors moves from the embedded Spec-IP shown in the preceding stage to the available matrix Spec-IP. Its pronounced NP occurrence is retained at the landing site, and an unpronounced NP trace replaces it at the source. These occurrences form an A-chain: the trace occupies the theta-position associated with reached, while the raised NP occupies the non-theta matrix subject position. The earlier subject theta-association is accordingly represented at the chain's foot. Finite matrix I licenses nominative on the chain's head and agrees with the plural subject, yielding the surface form seem rather than seems. The raised NP A-binds and antecedent-governs its trace across the transparent raising complement; no intervening CP or subject blocks this dependency. The trace representation is the GB movement representation, not a pronounced lower copy or PRO. Thus the derivation satisfies the theta criterion with one subject theta-role and supplies the overt subject with Case. The completed root is IP because no additional CP structure is required for this declarative input.
derivationStages.statement: Raise the sailors to matrix Spec-IP and complete the Case-licensed A-chain.

cases.name: german-embedded-auxiliary-1
cases.sentence: Lena vermutet, dass der neue Nachbar den alten Wagen reparieren wird.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The analysis uses head-final German IP and VP, a head-initial CP, and the traditional GB representation of nominal arguments as NPs. Determiners occupy Spec-NP; the attributive adjectives adjoin to N′. The embedded object precedes reparieren inside VP, and the finite future auxiliary wird occupies I. The embedded subject originates in Spec-IP, the external theta-position assumed here, rather than moving from a VP-internal position. Reparieren assigns the agent role to der neue Nachbar and the theme role and accusative Case to den alten Wagen; wird licenses nominative Case on the embedded subject. Dass heads the embedded CP and prevents the embedded clause from undergoing matrix-style verb-second movement. In the matrix clause, Lena occupies the external argument position, and the embedded CP is initially the selected complement preceding vermutet in the head-final VP. Vermutet assigns an experiencer role to Lena and a propositional-content role to the CP. Abstract finite I licenses matrix nominative Case and carries present-tense, third-person singular features. Vermutet is entered as the whole inflected lexical word: the silent grammatical features do not constitute separately pronounced morphological pieces. An initially empty matrix C provides the target for subsequent verb-second movement. This underlying workspace is not yet the surface word order.
derivationStages.statement: Establish the underlying clause structures, argument positions, and grammatical licensing.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The dass-clause moves from the complement position already represented inside the matrix VP to a right-adjoined position on matrix IP. A silent CP trace remains in its selected argument position. This analysis therefore treats the pronounced content clause as occupying the German Nachfeld, not as a freely attached explanatory adjunct. Its propositional theta-role remains associated with the complement position through the extraposition chain. The embedded clause moves intact: its complementizer, subject, object, infinitive, and final auxiliary retain their internal organization. Extraposition is represented before head movement so that the source and landing positions are explicit.
derivationStages.statement: Extrapose the selected content clause into the matrix right periphery.

cases.name: japanese-relative-7
cases.sentence: 先生が昨日読んだ本を学生が借りた。

values.interpretation: The book expression is the theme of borrowing.
The student is the agent of borrowing.

values.subjectPosition: The subject remains at its external-argument position.

values.morphologicalAnalysis: The vowel-stem verb 借りる combines with past -た.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge the accusative book expression with 借りる as its internal argument. Merge transitive little-v, introduce 学生が as the external argument, and then merge matrix past tense. Little-v licenses the object's accusative case, while tense licenses the student's nominative case without subject raising. Realize 借りる and past -た jointly as 借りた; the input pieces 借り and た therefore correspond collectively to those two syntactic heads. The resulting structure has subject–object–verb order. It is deliberately retained as an intermediate workspace because the pronounced input instead places the entire object before the matrix subject.
derivationStages.statement: Construct the matrix clause in its argument order and establish 借りた.

values.interpretiveCommitment: The fronted object retains its internal-argument interpretation; no contrastive-topic interpretation is required.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Internally merge the entire accusative book expression at the outer edge of the matrix tense projection, above 学生が. This clause-internal scrambling derives the input's object–subject–verb order; it does not move anything out of the relative clause. Adopt a trace representation for the displaced object: its former argument occurrence becomes a silent categorical trace, while the upper occurrence retains the complete relative nominal and its pronunciation. The two object occurrences share an identity, and the lower trace preserves the object's thematic and case dependencies. Because the target is within the matrix clause, this movement is completed before matrix phase transfer and requires no additional pronounced or intermediate position. Finally merge a silent declarative complementizer. Both past-tense realization associations persist in the completed structure. The result means that the student borrowed the book that the teacher read yesterday; the orthographic final punctuation has no supplied token and is not represented as a syntactic terminal.
derivationStages.statement: Scramble the matrix object leftward and complete the declarative sentence.

cases.name: english-passive-question-4
cases.sentence: Which report was the journalist believed to have misquoted?

derivationStages.stageRecord: Select and merge perfect have above the embedded v object, then select and merge infinitival to above the resulting Perf object. Perfect have selects the participial embedded predicate, yielding have misquoted once silent copies are disregarded. Infinitival T is defective for Case and does not supply nominative to the journalist. The selected infinitive is a T object without an intervening CP; this is the transparent raising complement required by passive believed in this analysis.
derivationStages.statement: Add perfect aspect and infinitival tense.

derivationStages.stageRecord: The infinitival T carries a subject-edge requirement but cannot value structural Case. Internally merge the journalist from its v-edge position at the edge of infinitival T. Its new occurrence is pronounced and its thematic occurrence becomes an unpronounced copy. This movement does not cross another subject: Which report occupies an A-bar edge and is already accusative, whereas the journalist is the eligible subject for this A-dependency. The subject must still obtain Case from the matrix clause.
derivationStages.statement: Raise the embedded subject to the infinitival T edge.

cases.name: english-passive-question-6
cases.sentence: Which report was the journalist believed to have misquoted?

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge believed with the infinitival T object, then merge unpronounced passive Voice above it. Believed takes the embedded proposition as its complement; it assigns no matrix theta-role to the journalist. Passive Voice supplies an implicit believer and does not license an accusative matrix subject. This passive Voice is not a strong phase blocking raising or wh extraction. Merge finite auxiliary T, realized as was, above Voice. Its probe reaches the still Caseless journalist at the infinitival T edge, values nominative Case, and establishes singular agreement. Was expresses the finite past auxiliary in the passive configuration; its surface position has not yet been derived.
derivationStages.statement: Build the matrix passive and establish finite agreement.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Following finite Agree, internally merge the journalist from the infinitival T edge at the matrix T edge, satisfying the finite subject requirement. Retain both earlier subject occurrences as silent copies and pronounce the new matrix occurrence. The subject is therefore interpreted as the agent of misquoting, not as the believer. The wh object remains at its embedded phase edge, and the finite auxiliary remains in T, so neither interrogative dependency has yet reached its final position.
derivationStages.statement: Raise the journalist into the matrix subject position.

cases.name: english-passive-question-8
cases.sentence: Which report was the journalist believed to have misquoted?

derivationStages.stageRecord: Select an unpronounced interrogative C and externally merge it with the completed matrix T object. C requires the finite auxiliary, so internally merge was from its previously established T position into a complex C head. The higher auxiliary occurrence is pronounced and its T occurrence becomes silent. The resulting head precedes the matrix subject, deriving was the journalist. C also bears the wh requirement that will attract the independently available wh object in the next stage.
derivationStages.statement: Introduce interrogative C and derive auxiliary inversion.

values.interpretation: ask which report the journalist was believed to have misquoted

derivationStages.stageRecord: Interrogative C attracts Which report from the embedded v phase edge to its own outer edge. The intervening infinitival T and passive Voice do not constitute additional strong phases in this analysis. Pronounce the new C-edge occurrence and silence the intermediate v-edge occurrence, retaining the original object copy as well. C establishes interrogative scope over the report variable interpreted in the complement of misquoted. The completed structure has two distinct movement chains: the journalist raises through infinitival T to matrix T, while Which report moves through the embedded v edge to C. With the auxiliary pronounced in C and all lower copies silent, the terminal order is exactly Which report was the journalist believed to have misquoted.
derivationStages.statement: Complete the wh dependency and the root question.

cases.name: english-island-1
cases.sentence: Which novel did Ada hear the rumor that Bea had translated?

derivationStages.stageRecord: Using an NP-based version of GB and X-bar theory, construct the interrogative NP Which novel as the complement of V, and project the embedded VP, IP, and CP. Bea occupies Spec-IP; finite perfect auxiliary had occupies I; translated is the participial lexical verb. That occupies C. The interrogative NP receives its Theme role and accusative Case in the embedded object position. This is the position from which its subsequent movement must originate. The initial workspace is an underlying constituent structure, not yet the input's surface order.
derivationStages.statement: Construct the embedded clause with the interrogative noun phrase in the object position of translated.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Move Which novel from the previously represented object position to embedded Spec-CP, leaving an unpronounced NP trace as the complement of translated. This models successive-cyclic A-bar movement rather than an unsupported direct leap from the object position. The moved NP retains the Case and theta-role established at its origin. Its presence beside overt that is an intermediate configuration: the NP will move onward, so the completed structure will not pronounce both a wh phrase and that in this embedded CP.
derivationStages.statement: Establish the embedded Spec-CP as an intermediate wh-movement position.

cases.name: english-island-4
cases.sentence: Which novel did Ada hear the rumor that Bea had translated?

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge the complex NP as the complement of hear, project the matrix VP, and place Ada in Spec-IP. Hear assigns its object role and accusative Case to the entire rumor NP, not to Which novel inside it. Matrix I is supplied by past-tense do-support, realized as did, while hear remains the bare lexical verb. Project a matrix CP with an unpronounced interrogative C. At this stage did is still in I and Which novel is still in embedded Spec-CP, providing explicit source positions for both remaining movements.
derivationStages.statement: Construct the matrix question before auxiliary inversion and final wh extraction.

derivationStages.stageRecord: First move did from matrix I to C, adjoining it to the interrogative head and leaving an I trace; this yields auxiliary-before-subject order. Then attempt to move Which novel from the previously established embedded Spec-CP to matrix Spec-CP, leaving an intermediate wh trace. These operations give the exact input order and a wh chain whose lowest trace is the object of translated. However, the second movement crosses both the containing rumor NP and matrix IP, the relevant bounding nodes in this NP/IP version of GB. It therefore violates Subjacency and the Complex NP Constraint. Successive cyclicity through embedded Spec-CP does not remove the intervening nominal island. The final tree records the attempted surface derivation and its failure, not a grammatical derivation licensed by standard GB. Overt that remains compatible with a silent intermediate trace; the decisive problem is extraction from the noun's content clause.
derivationStages.statement: Represent the exact surface sentence and identify its illicit complex-NP extraction.
